audit.report: The batch_replayable_fraud_model_rescore job (pid 1270424) held an idle-in-transaction lock for 4.2s with last statement SELECT 1, blocking 12 sessions and driving checkout to 0% success (120/120 failed over 30s) against a 95% SLO. The Database Guardian proposed termination because waiting would cost ~$4.4M in lost revenue (expected remaining runtime ~14,396s at $18,400/min) while terminating only incurs a 240-minute replay (policy permits interruption). The Continuity Guardian accepted as the 60s degradation tolerance was already exceeded. The pact closed in one round; the executor terminated the blocker and the verifier confirmed recovery: checkout 100% (36/36 over 10s), no lock waits, no protected operations aborted, in 155.6s total.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_fraud_model_rescore job entered an idle-in-transaction state (last statement SELECT 1) and held locks for 4.2s, blocking 12 checkout sessions and causing complete checkout failure.
lessons: Add fraud_model_rescore to the automated termination allowlist alongside email_digest_render and product_feed_rebuild, since memory shows terminating similar BATCH_REPLAYABLE jobs restores checkout to 100%.
Modify the fraud_model_rescore job (4-hour runtime, 240-min replay cost) to implement periodic commit/checkpointing so it cannot hold long idle-in-transaction locks that block checkout.
Investigate why the fraud_model_rescore worker enters idle-in-transaction with 'SELECT 1' and fix the application logic to release locks promptly after each batch.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians reasoned efficiently: the Database Guardian gathered all required evidence (lock blocker, workload registry, protected settlements, change calendar, business impact) in a single round, and the Continuity Guardian accepted immediately with no objections. No rounds were wasted, no evidence was missed, and no invariants were overridden.
follow_ups: Investigate why batch_replayable_fraud_model_rescore enters idle-in-transaction state with 'SELECT 1' and fix the application code.
